subject: Biotechnology
title: Defining Biotechnology
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Defining Biotechnology.

hook.text: Humans used living organisms as tools for 10,000 years — biotechnology is older than writing itself.

buildup.text: At its core, biotech means using biology to make useful products — from bread to insulin.

discovery.text: Modern biotech adds precision — we now edit genes, engineer cells, and design proteins on purpose.

twist.text: The term biotechnology was coined in 1919 by a Hungarian engineer — not a biologist.

climax.text: Today biotech spans medicine, agriculture, industry, and energy — one of the broadest fields.

punchline.text: Biology is technology — the oldest kind and the newest.

quiz.question: What does biotechnology fundamentally mean?
options: Using computers to simulate biological processes
Using living organisms or their components to make useful products
